The Hearth
Raised by semi-mythical lore-keepers.
Scavenger of memories and relics, sometimes haunted by them.
Dreamed of others’ deaths — perhaps as prophecy.
Believes gods are dead dreams that still influence the world.
Feared or revered by common folk without understanding why.
First met death when a Remnant stole his voice as a child
Believe an impossible claim
Elaron
The festival is the only time my stories
don’t feel like lies.
I’d die to keep that truth alive.
Grew up in a tower-city among wind and scrolls.
Seeks to explain even magic through logic and math.
Predicts omens and rituals through storm-reading.
Closest to death when lightning took her sister.
An eccentric known for storm omens and sharp truths.
Morally grounded but not always kind — direct and academic.
Take pity on the desperate
Thessaly
It’s a convergence of knowledge and meaning.
If it vanishes, generations lose their compass.
Be an agent of justice
Once a royal enforcer, now disgraced and wandering.
Prays to his sword more than the gods.
Scarred by killing his mentor at 19 to prevent a war.
Seen with a mix of fear and reverence by the public.
Believes gods are dead but dangerous.
Fears comfort and prefers the wilds or war camps
Kael
It’s the last place that welcomed me after
my fall.
If Emberwake burns, I burn with it.
Nimra
Nimra was raised in the flooded ruins beneath a decaying city
a child of tunnels, secrets, and survival.
She trades in whispers and favors, smuggling truths
where coin can’t reach. She believes in forgotten gods only
enough to leave offerings, just in case. Years ago, she watched
her sister drown for stealing a book, and she’s never stopped
searching for the meaning, or fighting against the meaninglessness
behind that moment
Extract a secret
it’s the only place no one tries to use her.
She can just be there — not a pawn, not
a spy. If it’s threatened, she’ll burn cities
to keep it hidden.
Iven Thorn
Iven was a prodigy in a hidden order dedicated to preserving
and obscuring dangerous knowledge.
A failed ritual scarred him and left him exiled, hunted by both
scholars and cultists. He believes gods were engineered
constructs — belief engines meant to control.
Now he roams from ruin to ruin, following forbidden texts and
impossible stories
Believe an impossible claim
the truth is there. Not just secrets, but
proof — of what was lost, of what could
be rebuilt. If it’s destroyed,
so is everything he’s worked for.
Garran Vael
Once a fortress commander during the Nine Woe Siege,
Garran sacrificed everything to save his troops.
Branded a traitor and stripped of his rank, he now
travels as a mercenary and reluctant folk hero.
He speaks old war prayers as mantras, not devotions.
Some still rally to him, but he fears what vengeance they want
him to bring.t
Break down a barrier
it’s the only place the next generation
has to stand and be free. If they lose it,
the cycle of conquest and silence
goes on
